candidates.rationale: Huber velocity loss should reduce the influence of rare extreme pose or occlusion outliers that dominate squared error while preserving smooth gradients for typical errors.
Depth coordinates are not directly observed in the 2D keypoints and are intrinsically harder to infer, so upweighting the z-axis velocity error should allocate more learning capacity to depth.
An auxiliary bone-vector loss on the implied clean pose should enforce limb lengths and directions, adding skeletal structure without changing the architecture.

Predicting the bounded clean pose internally and converting it to velocity should provide a better-conditioned target than directly predicting unbounded velocity, while preserving the external flow interface.
